problems.title: The KL threshold does not imply single-draw accuracy
problems.source_location: Proposition 2, PDF p.7; proof p.26; total-variation convention p.28
claim: The proposition asserts probability at least \(3/4\) of relative partition-estimator error at most \(\varepsilon\) when either path KL is at most \(\varepsilon^2/2\).
analysis: Use one masked coordinate with three clean states and common unmasking rate \(1/(1-t)\). Set proposal \(q=(1/4,1/4,1/2)\), target \(p=(2/5,1/10,1/2)\), and \(U_i=-\log p_i\), so \(Z=1\). The jump-time laws agree and path likelihood ratios are \(p_i/q_i=(8/5,2/5,1)\). For \(\varepsilon=1/2\), success occurs only in the third state, with probability \(1/2\). Yet \(D_{\rm KL}(p\Vert q)\approx0.0963724\) and \(D_{\rm KL}(q\Vert p)\approx0.111572\), both below \(1/8\). The full-support importance estimator is still unbiased.
result: The stated normalizer-accuracy guarantee is false in a valid masked process. Sampling quality and unbiasedness are separate claims and are not refuted by this witness.
repair: Under target absolute continuity, Markov and Pinsker give failure probability at most \[\sqrt{2\min(D_{\rm KL}(P\Vert Q),D_{\rm KL}(Q\Vert P))}/\varepsilon\]. The sufficient threshold \(\varepsilon^2/32\) recovers success probability \(3/4\).
problems.impact_rationale: An exact masked-process counterexample refutes a named central theoretical guarantee for normalizing-constant estimation.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Potts baseline collapses match counts into Boolean presence
problems.source_location: Eq.(18), PDF p.9; utils_potts.py, Metropolis energy calculation, lines 240–249, and Glauber update
claim: The Potts energy counts every matching neighboring spin. The release adds Boolean NumPy arrays without converting them to integer counts.
analysis: On a periodic \(3\times3\) lattice with three states, \(J=1,h=0,\beta=1.2\), change one spin in the all-zero configuration to state \(1\). Four matching edges disappear, so the correct Metropolis acceptance is \(e^{-4\beta J}\approx0.00822975\). Boolean addition retains one true entry instead of count four, giving \(e^{-\beta J}\approx0.301194\). All reverse one-site moves are accepted, so target-weighted incoming and outgoing fluxes at the all-zero state are respectively \(\pi(s_0)e^{-4\beta J}\) and \(\pi(s_0)e^{-\beta J}\); the target is not stationary for this kernel.
result: The released local sampler is wrong for the stated Potts target. Its exact contribution to published baseline tables requires code-to-run provenance; longer burn-in alone cannot fix the target mismatch.
repair: Cast each comparison to integers before adding, or stack and sum with an integer reduction. Use the resulting integer neighbor count in the Metropolis difference and Glauber conditional.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a release-level baseline-target mismatch; its lineage to the published comparison and corrected ranking remain unestablished.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: UDNS discretization and zero-time boundary lack valid domain conditions
problems.source_location: Appendix F.1, PDF pp.38–40; Algorithm 4 and Appendix F.3, pp.41–42
claim: The UDNS Euler kernel uses nonnegative learned scores and an early start near zero with \(\gamma(t)=1/t\), without an exit-rate step bound.
analysis: For the stated \(D=16,N=2,K=50\), choose \(\epsilon=1/1000\) and the reference score identically one. The first step has \(\Delta t=999/50000\); each flip probability is \(9.99\), and the stay probability is \(1-16(9.99)=-158.84\). Even the reference kernel needs \(\epsilon\geq4/29\). Separately, integrating \(1/t\) from zero gives immediate endpoint independence: \(\Pr(X_t\ne X_0)=1-N^{-D}\) at every positive time, incompatible with right continuity at zero. At finite \(\epsilon\), exact independence is lost; for a two-state target \((3/4,1/4)\), the uniformly initialized exact transformed process instead ends with first-state probability \(3/4-3\epsilon^2/[4(4-\epsilon^2)]\).
result: The literal extension is not a stochastic Euler algorithm throughout its declared score/start domain, and its singular initial path law needs separate formulation. This does not invalidate the distinct one-jump masked process.
repair: Enforce \(\Delta t\max_x[-Q_t(x,x)]\leq1\), with appropriate support restrictions for weights. Formulate the process from a positive initial time or an entrance law and rederive its boundary/weight statements; clipping probabilities alone does not restore them.
problems.impact_rationale: An explicit reference-score input makes the proposed extension assign negative probability, while the initial-boundary argument is invalid as a right-continuous path construction.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: A nonmemoryless reference can have a fixed-initial control optimum
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, PDF p.4; Lemma 8 and Remark 1, p.24
claim: The paper infers nonexistence of an SOC solution when the globally tilted path law fails the prescribed initial boundary.
analysis: For bounded finite-state rates and finite reward, define \(h_t(x)=E_0[e^{r(X_T)}\mid X_t=x]\). The conditional tilt \(dP^\dagger/dP^0=e^{r(X_T)}/h_0(X_0)\) preserves the prescribed initial law \(\mu\). For every admissible \(P\) with that law, \[J(P)=D_{\rm KL}(P\Vert P^\dagger)-E_\mu\log h_0.\] Thus it is the unique minimizing path law, regardless of endpoint independence. For the two-state rate-one switching chain, \(\mu=(1/2,1/2),T=1,e^r=(1,2)\), endpoints remain dependent and \(h_0=((3-e^{-2})/2,(3+e^{-2})/2)\) is nonconstant, yet this admissible optimum exists.
result: Incompatibility of a global tilt does not imply nonexistence of the constrained optimum. The deterministic masked initial state makes global and conditional normalization agree there, preserving that special construction.
repair: Use the conditional tilt and Doob rates \(Q^\dagger_t(x,y)=Q^0_t(x,y)h_t(y)/h_t(x)\), or explicitly assume \(h_0\) is constant on the initial support before using global-tilt marginals.
problems.impact_rationale: The source’s general existence/marginal argument confuses an infeasible unconstrained tilt with absence of a constrained optimum, a substantive SOC derivation error.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Released loss and reward normalizations differ from the estimators
problems.source_location: Eq.(16), PDF p.7; utils_train.py, loss_wdce, lines 72–94; rnd reward accumulation
claim: The release repeats softmax-normalized importance weights and then averages over the full batch; reward callbacks omit the displayed \(D\log N\) offset.
analysis: With normalized weights \(\omega_i\) and \(R\) remasking replicates, the stated self-normalized loss is \(\sum_i\omega_i R^{-1}\sum_r\ell_{ir}\). A mean over \(BR\) weighted entries instead returns this divided by \(B\). For the reward, subtracting \(\log N\) at every unmasking step while supplying only \(-U\) gives \(W_{\rm code}=W_{\rm paper}-D\log N\), so the expectation estimates \(Z/N^D\). At \(D=4,N=2,U=0\) with a uniform model, it returns weight \(1\) although the physical partition sum is \(16\).
result: These are normalization discrepancies. A fixed positive loss scale preserves ideal minimizers, and a common log-weight offset preserves normalized weights and ESS; neither proves wrong normalized samples or a published ranking reversal.
repair: Remove the extra batch averaging factor and state whether the estimated normalizer is a counting-measure partition sum or a uniform-reference expectation. Add \(D\log N\) when reporting physical \(\log Z\).
problems.impact_rationale: The release changes gradient and absolute-normalizer scales; central sampling quality and normalized ESS are not thereby refuted.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.
